reason: The auger is the only available action, and using it at the ice bank seems like a natural first step toward extracting water.
expectation: I expect the auger to extract or open access to the ice, though I’m unsure what form the result will take.

effect: The well produces a cloudy trickle, confirming that the ice is a water source but still needs treatment.
reaction: The heated probe melting ice beneath the dry cover was an interesting detail.
reason: The hose is the only available combination, and it seems useful for carrying water from the well toward the processor.
expectation: I expect the hose to connect to the well, though it may take another step to reach the processor.

effect: The hose now connects the well to the processor, completing the water delivery goal; the remaining task is to make the water potable.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the connection completed, though the step was straightforward.
reason: Using the connected line at the water processor is the only available combination and should advance treatment.
expectation: I expect the processor to draw and treat the well water, although I don’t know whether it will be potable immediately.

effect: The processor filtered grit, removed dissolved contaminants and checked the output, completing the potable water goal.
reaction: The nearly tasteless first cup was a satisfying payoff for turning a cloudy trickle into drinking water.

mostWorthwhile.text: Processing the water was most worthwhile: it connected the practical goal to the distinct jobs of removing grit, removing dissolved contaminants and checking the result.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the hose was straightforward and had only one available combination, so it offered little decision-making.

surprise.text: I was interested that the probe warmed ice beneath a dry cover and produced a cloudy trickle rather than immediately usable water.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary; each had a clear role in extracting, carrying or treating the water. The choices were nevertheless dictated by the available combinations.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because I am curious how the expedition develops and liked the concrete details about obtaining and treating water, even though this chapter offered few decisions.
